root_cause: The independent reference was wrong, not the implementation. It modelled a UNORM target as a float blend with only the stored code rounded (ENCODE 0.67, read back exactly). Vulkan and D3D11.3 both let a fixed-point target blend at its own precision, and llvmpipe and WARP blend UNORM8 targets in 8-bit integers: the premultiplied source and the alpha are converted to codes, the destination product d*(255-a)/255 is rounded, and the sum saturates. Each step rounds by up to half a code, so one blend moves up to 1.5 codes from the float blend; two partial blends (a label shadow, then its text) reach 2 codes outside the float-only interval. The shader cannot set output-merger precision; its output already follows the contract, and Metal stores the exact model bit for bit.

arithmetic.blend_type: lp_state_fs.c lp_blend_type_from_format_desc: R8G8B8A8_UNORM blends as 8-bit unsigned norm; sRGB formats (format_expands_to_float_soa) blend as float32
arithmetic.conversion: lp_state_fs.c generate_unswizzled_blend -> lp_build_conv_auto -> lp_bld_conv.c special case 2x8x32->16x8 (AVX): min(1,x)*255, lp_build_iround (llvm.x86.avx.cvt.ps2dq.256, round half to even), saturating packs; RGBA8 has_alpha, so the blend alpha is the converted alpha channel
arithmetic.blend: lp_bld_blend_aos.c: factors ONE / INV_SRC_ALPHA (comp = bitwise not); lp_bld_blend.c lp_build_blend generic path (not complementary): lp_build_mul(src, one)=src, lp_build_mul(dst, ~a) via lp_build_mul_norm, lp_build_add = llvm.uadd.sat
arithmetic.mul_norm: lp_bld_arit.c lp_build_mul_norm: (t + (t >> 8) + 128) >> 8; exhaustively: correctly rounded except 24 of 65,536 8-bit products (fraction 128/255, rounded down), max error 128/255 code

specifications.d3d11_3_3_2_3_6: "Convert from float scale to integer scale: c = c * (2^n-1). Convert to integer: c = c + 0.5f. Drop the decimal fraction ... This conversion is permitted tolerance of 0.6f ULP (on the integer side)."
